text:
Rest areas at closing stayed on our minds, and it was good to get your second message. We understand that your complaint is about the care, access, and follow-through you expected for your animal during the travel process. We are sorry that the experience left you frustrated, and we know that when a companion animal is involved, even small lapses can feel much larger.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk has reviewed the handling notes and spoken with the staff who supported the trip. The senior coordinator oversees these daily service decisions, and the supervisors are expected to listen carefully whenever a passenger raises a concern. In this case, we see that the concern was not handled with the clarity or pace that Aurelia Skyways aims to provide. That is not the standard we want set for you or for any traveler relying on our guidance.

We have already reinforced the basic steps with the team so that updates are given more clearly, handoffs are tracked more carefully, and special-care requests are not left to assumption. We also reminded staff that a calm, direct response matters when an animal's welfare is involved. This kind of work is routine for us, but the standard is not routine. It must stay high every day.

If there was a missed detail in the preparation or at the handoff point, we are treating that as a service failure, not a minor inconvenience. Your report helps us correct the process, and it will be used in our internal review. We want the next contact with the Companion Animal Travel Desk to feel steady, informed, and respectful from the start.

We appreciate that you took the time to write in again, and we regret that you needed to do so. Please be assured that your concern has been recorded and routed through the proper service channel for follow-up. We will continue working to make our support more reliable for you and for any future companion animal travel.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
